newsitem.title: USA: Mostly dry weather aids Missouri corn harvest.
newsitem.headline: Mostly dry weather aids Missouri corn harvest.

text.p: Mostly dry weather during the week ended September 1 allowed the corn harvest to start across the northern two-thirds of Missouri, the Agricultural Statistics Service said in a weekly crop update.
Ninety-six percent of the corn crop reached the dough stage or beyond, 79 percent reached the dent stage and 32 percent reached maturing, all ahead of last year and the five-year averages.

Six percent of the crop has been harvested versus five percent normally. About 25 percent is harvested across the southern third of the state, while harvest is just beginning across the rest of Missouri.
The crop is least advanced in the northeastern district where 81 percent of the crop reached the dough stage, 38 percent was denting and five percent was mature.
Corn was rated one percent very poor, six poor, 27 fair, 47 good and 19 excellent, similar to a week earlier.
Ninety percent of the soybean crop is setting pods, ahead of last year and one day ahead of the five-year average of 88 percent.
Soybeans were rated three percent very poor, 11 poor, 31 fair, 46 good and 9 excellent, similar to a week ago.
Ninety-six percent of the sorghum crop is heading or beyond, ahead of last year's 89 percent and the 95 percent average.
